source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (e-Nabavki) — Public Access portal
why_relevant: Legally mandated single publication channel for all North Macedonian public procurement: notices (огласи), tender documentation, award/contract notices (известувања за склучен договор), cancellations and realized contracts. Every state-body, municipality, public enterprise and state-owned bank tender for POS terminals, card personalisation, ATM/cash handling, core banking or payment software must appear here. This is the densest primary source for the A2 workstream in MK.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Реализирани договори / Institution grid data (contract realisation register)
why_relevant: Per-institution grid of concluded and realized contracts — lets you pivot from a contracting authority (e.g. a ministry, Фонд за здравствено осигурување, a state bank) to every contract it signed, including actual realized values versus contracted values. Key for sizing incumbent vendors in payments/IT lots.

source_name: ЕСЈН „Отворени податоци" — open-data export of concluded contracts
why_relevant: The BJN/ESJN has stated it publishes concluded-contract data in a machine-processable format downloadable in one click, with a redirect link from data.gov.mk. If confirmed live, this is by far the cheapest bulk-collection route for MK award data, replacing page scraping.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (BJN) — Bureau for Public Procurement
why_relevant: System owner and regulator of ESJN. Publishes the legal framework, annual procurement reports, 'red flags' risk reports, handbooks for ESJN and e-Pazar, model tender documentation and technical-specification templates. Best pointer for understanding how MK tenders are structured, which CPV/quantities are used, and where the aggregate statistics live.

source_name: BJN — „Годишни извештаи" (annual public procurement reports)
why_relevant: Aggregate market sizing: annual totals of procedures, values, procedure types and category breakdowns for the whole MK public procurement market. Provides denominators against which banking/payments lots can be sized.

source_name: BJN — „Red flags" извештаи (procurement risk-indicator reports)
why_relevant: Regulator's own irregularity/risk monitoring — single-bid procedures, tailored specifications, repeated winners. Useful for flagging which payments/IT lots are effectively pre-wired to an incumbent and where competitive entry is realistic.

source_name: e-Пазар (ePazar) — electronic marketplace for small-value procurement
why_relevant: Below-threshold purchases (small POS/card-reader batches, receipt paper, terminal maintenance, small software licences) run through the e-Pazar module rather than full open procedures, so a register built only from open tenders systematically misses this long tail. The BJN user manuals document the module's structure and access path.

source_name: BJN Прирачник за користење на ЕСЈН за економски оператори (ESJN user manual)
why_relevant: Documents the ESJN data model — notice types, dossier structure, search filters, statuses — which is exactly the schema a scraper must mirror. Cheapest way to design a robust collector without reverse-engineering the UI blindly.

source_name: Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (DKZJN) — State Commission for Public Procurement Appeals
why_relevant: Appeal decisions reveal the contested internals of tenders: disqualification grounds, technical-specification disputes, who bid against whom, and annulled/re-run procedures. For payments lots (POS, card personalisation, ATM services) the appeal file is often the only place bidder identities and evaluation detail become public. Annual reports give volumes by contracting authority.

source_name: Државен завод за ревизија (DZR) — State Audit Office, audit reports by auditee
why_relevant: Audit reports on individual institutions (including the National Bank and the appeals commission itself) routinely dissect procurement procedures: contract values, whether procedures were justified, direct negotiations, IT/payment-system spending. Reveals contract detail that never appears in the notice text, and identifies which authorities are heavy repeat buyers.

source_name: Народна банка на РСМ — Јавни набавки page
why_relevant: The central bank is the single most payments-relevant contracting authority in MK: cash processing and sorting machines, banknote handling, currency, RTGS/payment-system software, HSMs, IT infrastructure. It maintains its own procurement page (notices, concluded contracts, realized contracts) mirroring the ESJN entries — a low-volume, high-signal feed.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Јавни набавки / Склучени договори section
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the parent of BJN and the Treasury; its own contract listings cover treasury/payment-system IT, and its e-procurement section is the authoritative explainer of the ESJN's legal role. Doubles as pointer and as a direct source for a payments-relevant buyer.

source_name: Влада на РСМ — Јавни набавки / Отворена влада section
why_relevant: Government-level index of procurement transparency commitments and per-government-body procurement links; useful for enumerating the population of contracting authorities (договорни органи) to monitor, and for tracking policy changes to publication obligations.

source_name: Портал за отворени податоци — data.gov.mk
why_relevant: National open-data catalogue; the stated redirect target for ESJN's machine-readable contract exports and a route to adjacent datasets (budget execution, institution registries) that let award notices be joined to spending data.

source_name: Центар за граѓански комуникации (CCC) — public procurement monitoring programme
why_relevant: The most established independent MK procurement watchdog. Publishes twice-yearly monitoring reports and case-study series ('Јавен надзор над јавните набавки') that name specific contracts, winners, single-bid rates and confidential/annexed contracts. Frequently exposes contract detail the notice text omits, and its analysis frames which sectors are competitively contestable.

source_name: ЗаНабавки.мк (zanabavki.mk) — procurement practitioner/training resource
why_relevant: Practitioner-oriented MK procurement resource with training material on appeal procedures and procedural mechanics. Useful for glossary building and for understanding deadlines/thresholds that govern how quickly a notice must be captured.

source_name: TED / EU Publications Office — North Macedonia procurement notices (EU- and IFI-funded)
why_relevant: MK is not an EU member so domestic tenders do not go to TED, but EU-funded (IPA), EBRD and other IFI-financed procurements in North Macedonia are published there in English — including financial-sector programmes (e.g. an EBRD 'Financial and Operational Performance Improvement Programme, Skopje' notice was found). These are typically the larger, more strategic banking/payments modernisation projects and are entirely missed by an ESJN-only collector.

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators covering North Macedonia (GlobalTenders, TendersInfo, MacedoniaTenders, TenderImpulse, SellToState)
why_relevant: Paywalled English-language resellers of ESJN content. Not a substitute for the primary source, but useful as (a) a cross-check that a notice exists when ESJN blocks a fetch, (b) an English-translated CPV/keyword index that makes discovery easier, and (c) evidence of which MK tenders foreign vendors are actually tracking. Contract-award sections are the most useful part.

source_name: US ITA Country Commercial Guide — North Macedonia: Selling to the Public Sector
why_relevant: Concise English overview of how the MK procurement system works for foreign vendors — thresholds, e-Nabavki mechanics, typical barriers. Good orientation document and a sanity check on the legal framework, refreshed annually.

source_name: Institutional mirror pages of contracting authorities (ministries, municipalities, funds) — e.g. Министерство за одбрана, Министерство за дигитална трансформација, Општина Кратово
source_subtype: contracting-authority mirror pages / annual procurement plans
why_relevant: Many договорни органи republish their own notices, annual procurement plans (годишен план за јавни набавки) and concluded contracts on their own sites — sometimes with attachments and plan-level forward-looking detail that the ESJN record lacks. The annual plans are the earliest signal of an upcoming banking/payments/POS purchase, months before a notice appears.

source_name: Агенција за заштита на правото на слободен пристап до информациите од јавен карактер (ASPI) — FOI route
why_relevant: Maintains the register of information holders (иматели на информации) with their FOI officers' contacts. Provides the legal fallback for obtaining contract texts, bidder lists or e-Pazar data that the ESJN does not publish, and confirms which body to address for each authority.

source_name: Ministry of Finance RNM — Public Procurement section (Јавни набавки)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the top budget user and the owner of the Treasury; its own procurement section carries plans, notices and contracts for IT, payment and banking-adjacent services before/beside the central ESJN portal.

source_name: Ministry of Finance — Annual Public Procurement Plans (Годишни планови за јавни набавки)
why_relevant: Annual plans are the earliest legally-published signal of intended purchases (payment services, card issuing, POS, treasury banking, IT) — months before a tender notice appears.
